📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chapter 2 of GTA 6 finally gives you full control over both Jason and Lucia, and one of the first missions you'll undertake as a criminal couple involves committing a robbery in one of three locations.

One of your options is Avery Pawn Shop, where you'll be able to make a tidy sum of money if you can smash-and-grab enough loot and, more crucially, find the safe code to crack it open for additional cash and jewellery.The easiest way to do that is to grab the code for the safe, which is thankfully pretty easy to do.

Head inside Avery Pawn with your partner in tow—don't forget to pop on a mask, along with a hat and sunglasses to hide your identity—and begin holding up the store by pulling out your gun with L2 and pointing it at the clerks.

You should be able to threaten one of the staff members with Square and, with the other, the same input should instead change to "Safe Code?" if you look at the bottom-right corner. For me, it was the one standing behind the counter on the left.

The clerk should give up the safe code with little resistance. Once you have it, head behind the counter and into the back room. There'll be another staff member there, but you can point your gun and threaten him as well. Head into the office to the right, input the safe code, and grab your goods.

In a recent development, it looks like, at least where pawn shops are concerned, the code given is random. In my case, the code was 5683, but yours will most likely be different. This method should work for every pawn shop though, not just Avery Pawn!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that the location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection.

Sources indicate that by following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway.

Industry observers note that look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through.

It has been revealed that you can then drive away in your upcoming GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon.

Don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. However, the tank will eventually run out of fuel or become so damaged that it is completely incapacitated, and as surrender is no longer an option the upcoming Wasted is unavoidable.

The Wanted Level you get won't affect your current GTA 6 criminal profile, though you can only get a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 if you go all in on a psychotic rampage!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Industry observers note that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the tech giant trumpeted that their "fresh operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up upcoming possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot mentioned.

Sources indicate that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec stated. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing strategy with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

In a recent development, that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the firm affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

It has been revealed that we already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'Newly introduced Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

According to recent reports, here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 launched at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In a recent development, in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Upcoming Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

Amusingly, Upcoming Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Industry observers note that some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Recent findings suggest that kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Recent findings suggest that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you revealed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

In a recent development, last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

According to recent reports, I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

Industry observers note that this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

According to recent reports, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

Ubisoft cuts jobs at major Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios as its year of layoffs continues

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously declared operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
  • GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.
  • The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously declared operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture revealed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

In a recent development, "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

These latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" revealed by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • World of Warcraft: Forever's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive newly introduced lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly.
  • According to recent reports, mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

World of Warcraft: Forever's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive newly introduced lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly.

According to recent reports, mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit. I'll have a guild, friends I roleplay with, sure. But I'm very rarely striking up conversations with people in-game—all of that typically happens in Discord. And yet, here I am in WoW forever, trying to emphatically start conversations with goddamn everyone I meet.

According to recent reports, and it's in part because of how much of a bastard the game is. I don't think Classic is a particularly difficult videogame—I've even gotten my warrior from level 1 to, at the time of writing, 56 as fury, a spec typically considered trash for levelling. And it's been fine, I've just minded my pulls and levelled first aid.

It has been revealed that but it is a known fact that vanilla WoW quests are just easier when you group up with people. Part of this is because players are a force multiplier—many classes have group buffs, and not having to worry about health with a healer present means that you can pull swathes of enemies and melt them down easily.

And so I've been doing that. I've been grouping with people, and they've been grouping with me, and… oh, god, we've been talking to each other.

I don't know if I just happen to have a lucky propensity for drawing in nice folks, but my levelling journey has been dappled with some of the chillest people you'll ever meet. People hanging around to help you finish quests they've already completed is so common it's almost standard.

In one instance, a shadow priest carried me through multiple elite quests in Stranglethorn Vale—they needed to do 'em too, sure, but they actively went out of their way to show me where I could get a couple.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, there is a real, tangible sense of camaraderie in the game right now, one that's yet to be grinded to the marrow by the efficiency-laden tasks of Mythic+ or a seasonal system. But it's also one borne of how long everything takes. When you've already spent 10 minutes jogging to a quest, what's another five to help a stranger out?

It is, to put it plainly, the opposite of what I'd expected after years of playing far more modern MMOs. I'm even way ahead of the curve of the general population level-wise, and I'm still meeting these relaxed, generous folks. People who'll offer up scraps of a treasure map that's dropping from the pirates we're grinding for free, rather than being a mercenary about it and selling them on the auction house.

It has been revealed that moreover, it is infectious. I've been handing mana potions to people. I've been sticking around to help out with quests—in a recent Zul'farrak run, a dungeon I was only doing twice because I'd missed that it was required for the Sunken Temple questline, our tank had simply atrocious luck collecting troll tempers for a quest (you need 20 of them, and they don't drop often).

According to recent reports, not just myself, but another player in the same situation all stuck around for about 20 minutes just to help them out. When they thanked us, I, saccharine and glowing with the spirit of a reformed Grinch, said: "No worries, bud, if you wanna live in a village you've gotta be a villager sometimes.".

In a recent development, in short, Forever's turned me into a big, fluffy, golden-haired dog. The kind you meet in a park that bounds up to you with its stupid tongue wagging out. All that oldschool game design and camaraderie has, as it turns out, been a complete antidote to my hermetic ways. And while my street cred as a tough, solemn badass might never recover, I'm glad to be taking my time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • It has been revealed that that's now changing.
  • As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

It has been revealed that that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an important account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a new "View Once" option as well.

As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

As mentioned above, this feature is currently in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That mentioned, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

Recent findings suggest that if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest enhancement. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

  • Before the game's meteoric launch, Rockstar Games confirmed that its crime fest was locked at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S - the studio acknowledged that even the PS5 Pro wasn't capable enough to simulate the game's massive, complicated world at higher framerates, either.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some GTA 6 hopefuls weren't chuffed when hearing the open-world crime fest is targeting 30fps on all consoles, but there's actually a way to circumvent that framerate cap thanks to a newly-discovered glitch on Xbox.

Before the game's meteoric launch, Rockstar Games confirmed that its crime fest was locked at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S - the studio acknowledged that even the PS5 Pro wasn't capable enough to simulate the game's massive, complicated world at higher framerates, either.

But Redditor Mewwie64's has found a way to run the game with an unlocked framerate by using a Quick Resume glitch on Xbox Series X - that's the handy feature that lets you switch between games from where you last left off, without needing to boot up each one from scratch.

To run GTA 6 at 60fps or higher, you'll apparently need a 120hz display, an Xbox Series X, and the game itself on version 01.002.001. "This glitch may still work on later versions," the Redditor notes, "not sure.".

The dedicated player also gave interested folks a tutorial on how to up those framerate caps: "Put your Xbox display settings to 60hz. Start GTA 6. Wait until you see the six stars in the intro. Change your display settings back to 120hz. Cold boot another game on your console via the Xbox Guide (The Xbox button) and without quitting GTA 6. Switch back to GTA 6." And, voila.

Recent findings suggest that the Redditor does have one pretty major disclaimer, before you get too excited. "The game speed seems to be tied to your framerate," they write, so increasing the framerate might lead to certain animations looking faster than normal.

It has been revealed that "It seems like the animations are at 2x speed or more in Jason's house in Chapter 1. I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more. But when you exit the house everything runs at an increased speed (The game world is likely tied to your framerate) but cutscenes work 100% fine without problems on higher framerates. Only the gameplay is sped up." Be warned, then.

Nvidia's latest graphics card driver appears to be unnecessarily writing to PC SSDs, something that's dumb, annoying and definitely warrants reverting

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (361 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • According to recent reports, some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

According to recent reports, some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

It has been revealed that in order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any concerns and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand new arrival that the firm just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Sources indicate that here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar issue recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

Publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies announced. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates.

“With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat patch,” said Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release.

Here is an overview of the patch, via GRYPHLINE:.

Version Update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms”.

Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend?

Industry observers note that A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates.

In a recent development, the Old Dam, the update’s latest area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart.

The update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world.

It has been revealed that later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns.

It has been revealed that for factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking.

A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island.

Recent findings suggest that the livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield, arriving in the upcoming year. Exiles have rolled out attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different.

In a recent development, the chapter’s first upgrade will add four new maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode.

Industry observers note that arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a newly introduced high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode.

Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5, PC via the official launcher, Steam, and Epic Games Store, iOS via App Store, and Android via Google Play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As reported by The Shanghai Observer and Automaton, authorities in Shanghai have arrested 13 people and seized an untold number of unauthorized model kits and figures based on pop culture properties like Final Fantasy. The cops were reportedly put on the trail by a suspect Tifa Lockheart figurine.

It has been revealed that police in Fengxian, a district of Shanghai, began receiving complaints in June. The Shanghai Observer showed pictures comparing a Play Arts Kai (Square Enix's premium figure line) Tifa with a seemingly less articulated counterpart in the same outfit. Reading through machine translation, it sounds like customers in the area bought these figures online expecting the genuine article.

Industry observers note that the leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

Sources indicate that I'm of two minds about this, personally: I'm generally pro-kitbashing, selling custom figures, and using proxies in trading card games. In the face of some seriously inflated pricing from official merch lines, bootlegs can often be more enticing than the real deal, particularly if they offer features you can't get from official products⁠—the added customization options from this arrested vendor actually sound weirdly pro-consumer.

But it certainly appears, at least from The Shanghai Observer's reporting, that these suspect figures were being presented as the genuine article to customers. Paired with the increased price vs. official merch, and I find myself soured on the whole operation. It may seem small and silly, but as we endure the Golden Age of Scams, it's weirdly nice to see scammers face some consequences somewhere.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.
  • The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn.
  • As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

Sources indicate that and that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game debuted in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Sources indicate that leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

According to recent reports, either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 debuted today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#131719. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1019 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • Recent findings suggest that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • In a recent development, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

Recent findings suggest that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

In a recent development, proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

In a recent development, as the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

Recent findings suggest that for the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

In a recent development, what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

In a recent development, now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

To be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

Recent findings suggest that however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Image and video detection is the fresh string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

Again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

According to recent reports, next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran indicated that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Sources indicate that increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

Can you free-roam after beating GTA 6?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.
  • Industry observers note that you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that no matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list, you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. So naturally you must be wondering if you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, or whether you need to pack everything in before hitting a point of no return.

I'm going to answer this question for you and, because I'm nice, I'm going to do so in the most spoiler-free way that I possibly can.

Industry observers note that you can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6, albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status, your criminal profile, whether you paid into family savings, and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index.

This means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a fresh save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch.

According to recent reports, from this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again.

The GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. So, long story short, you can free-roam after beating GTA 6, but expect to have that final mission sitting on your menu screen for the long haul.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a very rare experience for me, but the year is almost over and I’m still talking about a movie that came out months ago on the 2026 release schedule: Obsession. I think it’s excellent on so many levels, but I particularly haven’t been able to get Inde Navarrette’s haunting performance as Nikki out of my head.

Recent findings suggest that and, ever since I saw it, I’ve been saying I want to see Navarrette win an Oscar for it. As luck would have it, the breakthrough star is very much expected to get a nomination in the Best Actress category at this point in the race. But, now that I’ve seen her biggest competition in earning the golden trophy, wow, I have upcoming thoughts to talk out.

I’ve been looking around at Oscar prediction sites, and while Inde Navarrette is quite high on the prediction list, there’s another actress always ahead of her: Julianne Moore for The Debut. And look, I like Moore, but she’s won an Oscar before and has been nominated a total of five times. She couldn’t possibly be better than Inde, I thought. Now that I’ve seen The Debut, I totally get why she’s so heavily favored now.

According to recent reports, I don’t say movies are perfect too often, but The Debut is one of my few five-out-of-five ratings of the year. (Obsession and You Can See Everything are the other two). The movie comes from Jesse Eisenberg – who helped Kieran Culkin get his Oscar back in 2025 for his writing/directing effort, A Real Pain.

The Debut is a laugh-out-loud dark comedy about a woman named Mona, who is drained by living her life for her family. So, she decides to try out for a community play. Here’s the thing: she’s not very good, but when the original actress drops out during rehearsals, the director Jerry (played by Paul Giamatti) enlists her.

According to recent reports, the Debut takes you through Mona’s chaotic journey as she attempts to understand what it really means to be an actress. I won’t get into too many details, but she completely gives herself over to the role in nuanced yet hilarious ways that has her slipping over the edge in a really entertaining way.

According to recent reports, oddly, there’s a transformation to it that’s not unlike what Navarrette did with Nikki. But, not only is Julianne Moore incredible as Mona, this feels like exactly the sort of performance that would appeal to Oscar voters because it’s literally about acting.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So, who am I rooting for now? I wish I could give it to both of them! While I’m more torn than I was before, I’d still like to see Inde Navarrette win that Oscar, the most honorable for what I think is a generational horror performance we’ll be talking about longer than The Debut.

While Moore is the frontrunner right now, with Gold Derby favoring Moore along with just about every prediction site, it’s still early in awards season. Moore is loved and respected by Hollywood, but it’s worth pointing out that Inde Navarrette’s likability and charm are off the charts. She could win over voters as the season goes on. But hey, I also didn’t think Amy Madigan’s Weapons performance would win at the 2026 Oscars, and she won! But now if The Debut wins, I won't be fuming, because Moore is truly so good, too!

Industry observers note that the Oscars are on the 2027 winter TV schedule for Sunday, March 14. That’s four months from now. A lot could happen on the awards season trail. You can’t see The Debut in theaters quite yet, but it’s among upcoming A24 movies, with it set to hit theaters widely on Christmas Day. And Obsession is presently on Netflix.

#131715. Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1371 w)

Eight Hacks Every Tidal User Should Know

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change.
  • Download your playlist as a .txt file.
  • Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Industry observers note that download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sources indicate that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

According to recent reports, like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of fresh-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

It has been revealed that on Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Users can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

According to recent reports, tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

Industry observers note that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

Sources indicate that mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

My cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

It's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

According to recent reports, your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

It has been revealed that most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

It has been revealed that you have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

This isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal. In fairness, the naysayers are still many and vocal, but they were back then too, and it turns out Bethesda saw at least a few of their posts. In a chat with The Examined Game, Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. There was a lot of people who were Obsidian fans, who were like 'Bethesda's gonna screw it up, they're just gonna make it Skyrim, we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout', and there was a strong, vocal community that just hated that we were gonna make that game".

For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: Fresh Vegas from 2010.

"We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". It's true: people bloody loved Fallout 3 and still do, though there are of course still series fans who reject the game. "There's always going to be some diehard people that say 'Fallout 2 was the greatest Fallout game ever', but we tried our best to just not engage… because you're not going to win that argument.

"All you can do is make the best game you can and let that be your statement. And that's what Bethesda did".

Sources indicate that does the vitriol ever get to Bethesda and its devs? Unsurprisingly, yeah, a little. "Any time somebody states that the thing you're doing is, you know, fill in your blank for all the cuss words and the bad things… you feel like it's a statement about yourself. You have to divorce yourself from that [but] you can't help but take it a little bit personally. But it does make you want to prove them wrong. It does make you want to say 'I'm going to show you that this will work, that we can respect the franchise and make it better and make it our way, rather than the old way".

Spoilers for Sunrise on the Reaping are ahead! You can catch The Hunger Games prequel in theaters now.

In a recent development, ever since the novel Sunrise on the Reaping came out, there’d been rumblings about Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson reprising their Hunger Games roles in the book-to-screen adaptation of the prequel. Now, the film is out on the 2026 movie schedule, the original Katniss, Peeta and Haymitch came back, and watching their scene together at the end of the movie made me emotional.

I really think it’ll stick with me too, and as I continue to be sappy about seeing these actors together again as these beloved characters, Josh Hutcherson explained how it all came together.

Before we get into how these cameos happened, let’s talk about what happened on the major screen.

At the end of Sunrise on the Reaping, we see Haymitch go back to District 12, and he learns that his mom and brother have died. Not long after that, Lenore Dove dies too after eating poisoned candy. Defeated by all of this, Haymitch isolates himself in Victors' Village, and we start to see him transform into the cynical man we meet in The Hunger Games as he watches kids die year after year in the games.

It has been revealed that then, there’s a big time jump from Haymitch’s first lonely years at home to a time post-Mockingjay. At that point, Woody Harrelson takes over to play the victor, and we see him with Jennifer Lawrence’s Katniss and Josh Hutcherson’s Peeta as they gather together. Notably, it’s clear they’re finally living in a world with no Hunger Games. They all seem at peace, and after their interaction, Haymitch goes to sit with the geese.

Industry observers note that overall, it’s a hopeful ending to a truly tragic tale, because it highlights that even though it took decades, eventually, the games stopped. And it will stick with me, because knowing Haymitch found his people and was able to live on happily with them after everything he had to endure makes me incredibly happy.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that plus, seeing Jennifer Lawrence back as Katniss and Josh Hutcherson return as Peeta meant the world to me, a gal who literally grew up on The Hunger Games books and movies. Now, how did the original band get back together for this? Hutcherson answered the question on Happy Sad Confused, explaining that it was a pretty substantial secret for a while:.

It has been revealed that I heard nothing until the day Francis Lawrence called me in maybe early summer of last year or something. And he called me and was like, ‘I have top secret information I need to share with you.’ And my heart dropped because I was like, ‘I don’t know what’s going to happen. This could be literally anything.’.

Hutcherson quickly learned it was Sunrise on the Reaping, and the director was also quick to tell him that Lawrence and Harrelson had already said yes:.

Sources indicate that [He told me] he’d read the manuscript and that, at the end of the film, we appear as our current aged selves. And he was like, ‘I talked with Jen. I talked with Woody. They’re down. Are you down?’ And I was like, ‘I’ve been waiting for this day for 15 years.’.

When Hutcherson was asked what his texts with Lawrence looked like after they learned about this, he said it was “just all caps.” They really were so excited to reunite for this.

Then, the trio went to Germany for a week; they shot for “four hours,” according to the Peeta actor, and then they got to “hang out” and “catch up.” Many months later, they reunited for the Sunrise premiere too. So, all around, it sounds like it was a lovely experience.

Sources indicate that overall, I don’t think Sunrise on the Reaping works without this last scene. We need that sliver of hope that shows that everything Haymitch went through ultimately led to a good outcome. It also brings the story full-circle and all the way back to the first characters (and actors) we got to see in this universe.

Ocarina of Time remake producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi - the developer who also served as game director on Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom - noted as much in an interview with Game Informer, explaining that he's "very, very happy" to hear that the remake's finale is having an emotional affect on some players.

Industry observers note that "That cutscene – cutscenes in general – but that cutscene specifically is something that we, as a dev team, heavily discussed," Fujibayashi claims of the game's ending. "Because of the limitations of the technology back in the day, there might have been things that we weren't able to convey fully, whether it's because of the tempo of the game… whatever it is.".

Industry observers note that almost three decades of hardware improvements and technical know-how let Nintendo realize the scene fully, as it was first intended all those years ago on the N64. "And so, when we approached this remake, we wanted to make sure that we captured that moment in the way that we wanted to express it. So that the right kinds of emotions are evoked, and that we can convey the emotion and the story that we wanted to at that moment," Fujibayashi adds.

The Zelda maestro is just "really relieved to hear" people are having strong reactions to the end of the game and its full-circle send off.

Sources indicate that the Switch 2's Ocarina of Time seems to have been welcomed with glowing reactions across the board. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deciding whether to proceed or postpone the Protective Custody story mission is a substantial choice you'll need to make in GTA 6. The mission appears on your map as "Meet Abe" in Chapter 5, once you've completed the mission Operation Savage Glory.

In a recent development, once you get to Abe's office, Jason will warn Lucia that everything will change after this mission. Lucia will hesitate at the door as you make your choice to "Proceed" or "Postpone.".

According to recent reports, this is a pretty big decision, because Protective Custody kicks off the final mission of the game which takes about an hour to play. And even though it's a binary choice between "Proceed" (which starts the mission) and "Postpone" (which delays the mission)" there's actually a third possible outcome based on when you make the choice.

It has been revealed that it's a long mission that will take about an hour to play, so be prepared. You can't save during this mission so make sure you've got the time! Once you've completed the final mission, you can watch the credits and return to the open world so you can continue playing.

You will go back to the open world to continue playing. The "Meet Abe" icon will remain on your map so you can begin the final mission at any point from then on.

Industry observers note that there are multiple endings to GTA 6, and I won't spoil them here. But one of the endings is only possible if you postpone the Protective Custody mission until you've deposited $2 million into your Buck Me savings account. That's why when you choose to proceed with the final mission makes a difference.

It's also worth noting (again, without spoilers) that just because you do have $2 million in your Buck Me savings account does not guarantee you will see this particular ending. There are still choices you'll need to make in the final mission that determine which ending you see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I recently switched music streamers from Apple Music to Tidal. I like Tidal's strict anti-AI features, the fact that it pays higher royalties to artists than other major streamers, and its focus on high quality audio. I wrote a post featuring eight hacks for Tidal consumers, but I wanted to highlight one in particular: How to transfer playlists without paying anything.

It has been revealed that download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Sources indicate that install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

According to recent reports, run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sources indicate that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game
